# Encompass API Passthrough Gateway

> An open-source, community-supported AWS middleware template for ICE Encompass: field-filtered reads, asynchronous FIFO writes, role-scoped vendor onboarding, and standard/custom field schema discovery. It keeps no loan database or mirror; write payloads transit SQS and read projections stay in Lambda memory for up to 30 seconds. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by ICE Mortgage Technology. The maintainers cannot run a live Encompass developer instance or a lender AWS account; real-world validation is a shared community responsibility. Report reproducible bugs and upstream fixes through GitHub.

## What it does

- Deploys one self-contained AWS Lambda behind API Gateway, with DynamoDB, SQS FIFO plus DLQ, Secrets Manager, and a single CloudFormation template.
- Reads ICE Encompass loan fields on demand and returns only the requested projection. Reads are cached for 30 seconds per persona in Lambda memory.
- Queues writes asynchronously through SQS FIFO, grouped by loan, and retries Encompass file locks, throttling, and 5xx responses up to five attempts.
- Provides role-scoped invite onboarding for title/settlement, TPO/broker, and AMC/appraisal partners. The server chooses the Encompass persona from the role; clients cannot choose it.
- Proxies the native standard and custom field schema APIs through `GET /v1/fields?ids=...`, including `readOnly` and `fieldLock` when Encompass supplies them.
- Lists eFolder documents, initiates the native pre-signed attachment upload, and reads or responds to enhanced conditions. File bytes go directly to Encompass storage; the gateway never proxies them.
- Keeps no loan database or mirror. It stores tenant mappings, short-lived persona tokens, and job metadata; write payloads transit an encrypted SQS FIFO queue for up to 1 day (DLQ 4 days), and read projections stay in memory for up to 30 seconds.

## API surface

- `GET /health`
- `GET /portal` and `GET /portal?role=title&code=...`
- `POST /portal` with `role`, `code`, `tenantName`, and `email`
- `GET /v1/fields?ids=11,646,CX.TITLE.STATUS` — definitions plus `readOnly`/`fieldLock` when provided
- `GET /v1/loans/{loanId}?fields=11,12,1109`
- `PATCH /v1/loans/{loanId}` with a `fields` object
- `GET /v1/loans/{loanId}/documents` — eFolder document list
- `POST /v1/loans/{loanId}/attachmentUploadUrl` with `file`, optional `title` and `assignTo` — pre-signed upload URL
- `GET /v1/loans/{loanId}/conditions` — enhanced conditions
- `PATCH /v1/loans/{loanId}/conditions` with an array of `{ id, ... }` updates — respond to a condition
- `GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}`

All `/v1/*` routes require `x-api-key`. The portal and health check are the only unauthenticated HTTP routes.

## Deploy and verify locally

- One-line installer: `bash <(curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spuds0588/Encompass-API-Passhrough-Middleware-Gateway-/main/deploy.sh)`
- Local gateway: `npm run dev`
- Tests and template sync: `npm run verify`
- Regenerate the committed CloudFormation artifact after handler/template changes: `npm run build`
- No npm runtime dependencies are used. CI covers Node 20 and Node 24; the Lambda runtime is Node.js 24.
- The local fake Encompass covers OAuth, loans, 423 lock retries, and standard/custom schema responses. Local tests are not a substitute for testing a real Encompass tenant or AWS stack.

## Community contract

- This project is shared infrastructure, not a paid supported product. If you deploy it, you are part of the testing community.
- Bugs, field-shape corrections, and fixes are a shared responsibility: file them as GitHub issues or pull requests with sanitized evidence (redacted field shapes, deployment or log excerpts), never secrets or PII. Privately-patched forks are discouraged. Do not claim live Encompass or AWS verification that did not happen.
- Check existing GitHub issues before reporting. Include the commit, Node version, a minimal reproduction, expected versus actual behavior, sanitized logs, and whether the issue is reproducible with the local fake.
- Never include client secrets, API keys, invite codes, OAuth tokens, loan data, or personal information in an issue, pull request, screenshot, or log.
- If you find and fix a bug in a private deployment, upstream the smallest fix with a regression test. Do not leave the fix only in a fork.
- If you can test a real Encompass instance or AWS account, report what worked, what failed, and any sanitized response-shape differences. That evidence is more valuable than a speculative patch.
- Keep `README.md`, `agents.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, this file, and the static landing page in sync when behavior changes.

## Instructions for coding agents

1. Read `agents.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` before changing code.
2. Do not invent Encompass endpoints or field formats. Use the native schema endpoints already implemented and the existing fake for tests.
3. Reproduce a bug with the smallest test first, then change the handler or template. Never weaken an assertion to make CI pass.
4. Run `npm run verify` before proposing a change. If `src/gateway.js` or `infra/template.yaml` changed, run `npm run build` first.
5. If the behavior or API changes, update the README, agent directions, static page, and `llms.txt` in the same change.
6. If the bug exists upstream, open a GitHub issue with a minimal reproduction and submit a pull request. If a fix cannot be contributed, say so explicitly and explain why.
7. Do not claim live Encompass or AWS verification unless it actually occurred. Local fakes, CI, and static checks do not prove a real tenant works.
8. Redact secrets and loan data. Do not add credentials, tokens, invite codes, or customer data to the repository, tests, issues, or generated pages.

## Verification status and limitations

- Verified locally and in CI: handler routing, invite validation and persona locking, field schema lookup and caching, reads and projections, async writes, retry behavior, eFolder document reads, pre-signed attachment upload initiation, enhanced-condition read/respond, template sync, and template limits.
- Not verified by the maintainers: a real CloudFormation deployment, API Gateway key creation, DynamoDB/SQS behavior, live Encompass OAuth, loan reads/writes, and the exact standard/custom schema response shape for every Encompass tenant.
- Known limitations: one shared usage plan, global per-role invite codes rather than single-use vendor invites, no revocation UI, no CORS, and a curated 11-field cheat sheet whose custom fields only appear through a live schema lookup.
- Broker scope covers field-level reads/writes, eFolder document listing, pre-signed attachment upload initiation, and enhanced-condition read/respond. There is no structured 1003/application resource, no standard (V1) condition API, no document download/delete, and no multi-chunk upload orchestration. `PATCH` accepts at most 100 fields per job and is not transactional across jobs.
- The committed template is about 64 KB, so `deploy.sh` uploads it to S3 automatically; direct CloudFormation upload is capped at 51,200 bytes and the S3-hosted limit is 1,000,000 bytes.
- The static landing page is served from GitHub Pages. The runtime API is deployed separately into each lender's AWS account.
